source_text:
ἐγένετο ταῦτα, φησί, σκιὰ ἦν τῶν μελλόντων· ἡ δὲ σκιὰ προτρέχει τοῦ σώματος.
ἐπειδὴ τοίνυν ἡ σκιὰ τὰ νόμιμα, τί τὸ σῶμα; οὐ σκιὰ τὰ Χριστοῦ. ἐλθόντος οὖν τοῦ
σώματος, περιττὴ ἡ σκιά. Kol 2,18β Ποία ταπεινοφροσύνη; ἐν τῷ λέγειν ὅτι ἡμεῖς μὲν
ταπεινοί ἐσμεν, ὁ δὲ θεὸς μέγας καὶ ὑπερβαίνων τὸ ὑφ' ἡμῶν θεραπεύεσθαι. ἐπεὶ οὖν
μέχρις αὐτοῦ οὐ φθάνομεν, διὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ ἐξιλεούμεθα αὐτὸν καὶ
προσαγόμεθα αὐτῷ. καὶ ἀνωτέρω δὲ ἔλεγεν· ὅς ἐστι κεφαλὴ πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ
ἐξουσίας, καὶ νῦν φησιν· διὰ τί ἐπὶ τὰ στοιχεῖα καὶ ἀγγέλους ἔρχεσθε,
καταλελοιπότες τούτων τὴν κεφαλήν, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ὁ Χριστός; Ἐπειδὴ ἔλεγον ὅτι ὁ
θεὸς μέγας ἐστίν, ἀκατάληπτός ἐστιν, ἀόρατός ἐστιν, καὶ οὐ φθάνομεν ἐκεῖ. διὰ
τοῦτο ἐπειδὴ οὐ χωροῦμεν τὸν μέγαν, διὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων προσαγόμεθα. καὶ ταύτην
ταπεινοφροσύνην φησίν. Kol 2,19 Ἐντεῦθεν ἔδειξε τὸν σκοπὸν ὃν λέγομεν, ὅτι διὰ
τὸ τινὰς παραινεῖν δι' ἀγγέλων προσάγεσθαι, διὰ τοῦτο ἐκινήθη. δεῖ, φησί, τῆς
κεφαλῆς ἔχεσθαι· κεφαλὴ γάρ ἐστι τοῦ παντὸς ὁ θεὸς λόγος. τί οὖν ἀφεὶς τὴν
κεφαλὴν κρατεῖς τὸ σῶμα; κἂν γὰρ ἁρμονίας ἔχῃ λόγον συναπτούσης 326 δύο μέλη ἢ
πλείονα τῶν ἀγγέλων ἡ δύναμις. ἀλλ' οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κεφαλῆς ἔρχεται εἰς πάντας ἡ
ὠφέλεια, εἰς ἀγγέλους ὡς ἀγγέλους, εἰς ἀρχαγγέλους ὡς ἀρχαγγέλους, εἰς τὰ ὁρατὰ
ὡς ὁρατά. θές μοι τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀντὶ κεφαλῆς εἶναι τῷ κόσμῳ, ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμῶν ἥλιον
καὶ σελήνην, καὶ οὕτως ἕκαστον μέρος τοῦ κόσμου ἐν μελῶν τάξει συντιθείς,
εὑρήσεις ἓν σῶμα τοῦ παντός. καὶ καθάπερ ψυχὴ ἐν σώματι καὶ σῶμα ψυχῆς, οὕτω
τὰς ἀοράτους δυνάμεις ἐν τοῖς ὁρατοῖς. πάντων δὲ τούτων κυριωτέρα ἡ κεφαλή, ἀφ'
ἧς ἡ ὠφέλεια εἰς ὅλον ἔρχεται τὸ σῶμα, ἐπιχορηγουμένη δηλονότι ἀπὸ τῆς κεφαλῆς.
Kol 2,–22 Εἰ διὰ τοῦτο, φησίν, ἀποθνῄσκετε σὺν Χριστῷ, ὥστε μὴ τοῖς στοιχείοις τοῦ
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing the second catena form on Colossians 2:17] ... these things happened, he says, they were a shadow of the things to come; and the shadow runs ahead of the body. Since, then, the legal ordinances are the shadow, what is the body? The things of Christ are not shadow. So, the body having come, the shadow is superfluous.
Colossians 2:18b. What kind of humility? In saying that we are lowly, but God is great and goes beyond being served by us. Since, then, we do not reach as far as him, through his angels we propitiate him and are brought near to him. And higher up he was saying: "who is head of every rule and authority," and now he says: why do you go to the elements and angels, having left behind their head, which is Christ?
[Second form, unmarked repetition:] Since they were saying that God is great, he is incomprehensible, he is invisible, and we do not reach there. Therefore, since we do not contain the Great One, we are brought near through the angels. And this he calls humility.
Colossians 2:19. From here he showed the aim which we speak of, that because some were urging (people) to be brought near through angels, for this reason he was moved. One must, he says, hold on to the head; for God the Word is head of the universe. Why then, letting go of the head, do you hold the body? For even if the power of the angels has the role of a joint linking two members or more, still the benefit comes to all from the head: to angels as angels, to archangels as archangels, to the visible things as visible things. Suppose for me that the heaven is in place of a head to the world, in place of eyes sun and moon, and so, setting each part of the world together in the order of limbs, you will find one body of the universe. And just as soul in body and body of soul, so (you will find) the invisible powers in the visible things. But more sovereign than all of these is the head, from which the benefit comes into the whole body, being supplied, clearly, from the head.
Colossians 2:-22 (label damaged). If for this reason, he says, you die with Christ, so as not to worship the elements of [continues in the next section: this world]
pass_b_english: … Since, then, the ordinances of the law are the shadow, what is the body? What belongs to Christ is not shadow. So once the body has come, the shadow is superfluous.

On Colossians 2:18: What sort of humility? The humility of saying: “We are lowly, and God is great, too great to be served by us. Since we cannot reach as far as him, we win his favour through his angels, and through them we are brought to him.” Earlier he said, “who is the head of every rule and authority” (Colossians 2:10), and now he says: why do you go to the elements and to angels, abandoning their head, which is Christ?
The second catena form adds: … God is incomprehensible and invisible … since we cannot take in the Great One … And this is what he calls humility.

On Colossians 2:19: Here he made plain the aim we have been speaking of: what moved him to write was that some people were urging others to approach God through angels. We must, he says, hold fast to the head, for God the Word is the head of the universe. Why, then, let go of the head and cling to the body? The power of the angels may serve as a joint that links two or more limbs, but the benefit still comes to all from the head: to angels as angels, to archangels as archangels, to visible things as visible things. Picture the heaven as the head of the world and the sun and moon as its eyes. Arrange each part of the world in this way, as limbs in their order, and you will find one body of the universe. As there is a soul in the body and the body belongs to the soul, so you will find the invisible powers in the visible things. But the head is more sovereign than all of these, and from it the benefit flows into the whole body, supplied, of course, from the head.
On Colossians 2:20–22: If, he says, the reason you die with Christ is that you should no longer worship the elements of …

choices.term: ἐγένετο ταῦτα, φησί, σκιὰ ἦν τῶν μελλόντων· ἡ δὲ σκιὰ προτρέχει τοῦ σώματος.
choices.english: not printed; the section opens '… Since, then, …'
choices.why: Continues the second catena form of the shadow note (324,col2-325,col2) begun at the end of u02-open; this first sentence repeats the first form ('the shadow runs ahead of the body') and is dropped as a doublet. The next three sentences have no counterpart and are printed.
Edition label 2:18b, the 'humility' clause; given as 2:18.

choices.term: ὁ δὲ θεὸς μέγας καὶ ὑπερβαίνων τὸ ὑφ' ἡμῶν θεραπεύεσθαι
choices.english: God is great, too great to be served by us
choices.why: θεραπεύω = serve, attend on (worship); the old English 'surpassing being healed by us' was garbled (SOURCE_ISSUES item 5).
rejected: God is great and surpassing being healed by us

choices.term: Ἐπειδὴ ἔλεγον ὅτι ὁ θεὸς μέγας ἐστίν … καὶ ταύτην ταπεινοφροσύνην φησίν.
choices.english: Doublet collapsed (Colossians 2:18): reduced to 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: Unmarked repetition of the humility note. Added material kept: 'incomprehensible, invisible', 'we cannot take in the Great One', 'this he calls humility'.

The edition's label is damaged (start verse missing). The note paraphrases 2:20 ('if you died with Christ ... the elements of the world ... why ... subject to ordinances') and quotes 2:21–22, so it is labelled 2:20–22.

choices.term: Ἐντεῦθεν ἔδειξε τὸν σκοπὸν ὃν λέγομεν
choices.english: Here he made plain the aim we have been speaking of
choices.why: Refers back to the argument of the letter (u01-open); old English 'From there he showed the aim which we speak of, that because of some to exhort ...' was unreadable.

bible_refs.note: ὅς ἐστι κεφαλὴ πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας, cited as 'higher up'
